source.title: Learning from Data with Noisy Labels Using Temporal Self-Ensemble
source.authors: Jun-Ho Lee; J. Baik; Taebaek Hwang; J. Choi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy for a standard network trained on datasets with several synthetic label-noise rates, bearing on the test-performance part of V4. It does not measure training error or test complete random labeling.
record.gate_note: The paper's own Standard baseline results in Table 1 report test accuracy under synthetic label noise. Cited claims about memorization from prior work are not extracted as results. No training-error, complete-random-label, unstructured-input, or learning-order results are reported.
record.test_reason: The Standard baseline directly tests V4's test-performance component by varying symmetric label noise and measuring test accuracy. Perfect training-set fitting is unmeasured, so these results support only that component.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors conclude that SRT combines temporal self-ensembles and multi-view consistency to filter mislabeled samples and improve test accuracy over the evaluated comparison methods, while training a single network.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a noisy-label filtering and robust-training method using cyclical learning rates, temporal self-ensembles, and multi-view predictions. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracy varies with dataset and synthetic noise type and rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 shows Standard test accuracy rising early and declining later; the authors attribute the decline to memorization of incorrect labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under noisy-label training, held-out accuracy can improve early and deteriorate later. This trajectory alone does not establish that clean labels are fitted before noisy labels.

record.code_released: The source code will be publicly available.
record.problems: The paper does not report training error for the Standard baseline, so its test-accuracy results cannot establish whether the networks fit the corrupted training labels. The Jo-SRC comparison values were brought from the original paper rather than reproduced.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows. Table 1 reports test accuracy for Standard and robust-training methods under synthetic label noise, but none of those values alone measures the training-set fitting required by V4. Figure 3 reports test accuracy over epochs; it does not report training error.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels; the zero-noise and fully random endpoints. Only intermediate noise rates and test accuracy are measured.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
The learning order of clean and noisy training labels. Test-accuracy trajectories do not directly measure their respective fitting trajectories.

missing.what: Extract the Standard baseline's symmetric-noise test accuracies as evidence for V4's test-performance component. Although rows_left_out explicitly declares their omission, the stated reason is too restrictive: a result can bear on one component without establishing the entire version.
missing.locator: Table 1, Standard rows for MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100; Evaluation subsection specifies five runs and averaging over the last ten epochs.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to correct. Robust-training method comparisons and filtering metrics do not establish random-label fitting. Neither the absent training-error measurements nor the absence of fully random labels warrants a challenges or limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No complete random labeling condition or training error is reported.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed against the true-label condition is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.

The paper varies synthetic label-noise rates and reports test accuracy, but reports no training error or evidence that the training set is fit perfectly. Table 1 results are reported separately by dataset and noise condition; they are not extracted because test accuracy alone does not establish the version's claimed joint outcome.
No experiment tests whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether removing these methods changes true-label generalization.
No result measures the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned.

relationships.condition: Standard supervised training on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 with 20%, 50%, and 80% symmetric label noise; test-performance component only.
relationships.reason: From Table 1, absent from the rows: test accuracy decreases monotonically from 79.29 to 52.86 to 22.89% on MNIST, 69.46 to 42.62 to 16.18% on CIFAR-10, and 35.43 to 17.30 to 4.26% on CIFAR-100, approaching chance. Training-set memorization remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy declined toward chance from 79.29% to 52.86% to 22.89% on MNIST, 69.46% to 42.62% to 16.18% on CIFAR-10, and 35.43% to 17.30% to 4.26% on CIFAR-100.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
